A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DNC/UFM spectral research despite the shortened title in v3. Their text, equations, figures, and complete Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including matching reordered theorems and relocated experiments.

before.justification: v2 reports original deep-UFM simulations and neural-network experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10, including spectral, gradient-alignment, and effective-rank results in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulations and MNIST/CIFAR-10 analyses and adds MNIST results using a ReLU head with conventional regularization.

M1.justification: The linear and ReLU UFMs, MSE objective, and appendix CE model are retained. The added real-network configuration evaluates the existing theory; it does not introduce a new proposed method or model component.

E1.justification: Coverage remains deep-UFM simulations and MNIST/CIFAR-10 classification. The added MNIST experiment changes architecture and regularization within the same data and task coverage. CIFAR-10 alignment results move from v2 Figure 6 to v3 Figure 20.

E2.justification: Neither version adds competing empirical algorithms as baselines. Comparisons against analytical predictions and the same Hessian-decomposition components are retained; new theory reference lines do not introduce comparison methods.

E3.justification: v3 Figure 7 adds a MNIST configuration with ReLU fully connected layers and conventional parameter regularization at lambda = 0.005. The original linear-head, UFM-regularized experiments retain their sample counts, preprocessing, training budgets, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 checks whether spectral and alignment predictions persist when head activations and regularization depart from the original UFM-matched configuration. This jointly tests two modeling choices. Existing decomposition knockouts, feature/weight spectra, singular-vector alignment, and effective-rank analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions present individual runs and use one-standard-deviation summaries across class indices or outlier values. v3 does not introduce repeated-seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added plots follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 replaces the linear-UFM alignment traces and newly reports final agreement to eight significant figures for eigenvector alignment and five for gradient alignment in Figure 2. Figures 6–7 add MNIST spectral snapshots and ReLU/conventional-regularization outcomes. Existing appendix results and central outlier-count conclusions are retained.

T1.justification: Definition 2.1 changes DNC3 from individual-mean collinearity to general linear combinations. Theorem 6 becomes Theorem 3.6 with fixed expressive feature-map depth instead of the joint depth limit, and asymptotic block-scale assumptions are clarified. Previously discussed regularization decay becomes explicit in the theorem. Most spectral formulas and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that DNC unifies low-dimensional spectra through feature-mean expressions, explains gradient alignment, and connects layer-wise structure to the full Hessian, with linear/ReLU theory and empirical validation. The rewritten contributions emphasize these retained claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.4 discusses MSE applicability, fixed feature-map depth, asymptotic Hessian-block scaling, and evidence under conventional regularization. Appendix B refines the explanation of CE spike counts through orthogonal versus simplex feature geometry. These extend interpretation and assumption justification beyond v2.

D1.justification: Appendix G.2 newly states MSE use for real-network experiments and documents the added ReLU configuration's regularization strength and inherited training setup. Existing UFM hyperparameters and numerical conventions are largely relocated to Appendix G.1 and captions rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Bolshim and Kugaevskikh, Walter et al., Hui and Belkin, and Dang et al. (2024), while removing several broader NC citations, including Beaglehole et al. It adds practical layer-wise Hessian positioning and explicitly contrasts the two-layer scope of Ben Arous et al.; the central novelty position remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, conclusion, and substantial main-text prose are rewritten. v3 introduces a Contributions subsection, separates Hessian cross-class structure, reorders ReLU theorems and proofs, and integrates UFM experimental explanations into the theory sections while focusing Section 5 on real networks.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to two-column layout. Figures are reordered and recombined, several gain theory lines and clearer legends/captions, and the original combined MNIST/CIFAR-10 figure is split across main text and appendix. New MNIST spectrum panels and Figure 7 substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity through reorganized exposition, explicit theoretical reference lines, and more precise definitions and assumptions. Figure 7 adds useful practical validation beyond v2's linear-head, UFM-regularized experiments. The scientific gain is incremental: most proofs and results are retained, and the new experiment shows approximate agreement while jointly changing activation and regularization.
